focus_areas: Junction integrity between claws and body.
Count and symmetry of lateral walking legs.
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'left' claw (viewer's perspective). Does the texture transition from red to white look biologically plausible or digitally airbrushed? Verify if the eye stalks emerge from distinct sockets or if they appear to float on the shell surface. Check for any 'double edges' or ghosting around the serrated teeth of the claws. Crucially, count the visible walking legs on both sides to ensure they are structurally complete and not fused into the background or carapace.
image_description: A close-up, eye-level shot of a Dungeness crab (Cancer magister). The image focuses on the anterior portion, highlighting the broad, reddish-brown carapace and two large, robust chelipeds (claws) extended forward. The claws show characteristic white/cream coloring on the inner surfaces and red tips. Multiple walking legs are visible extending laterally from beneath the carapace on both sides. The eyes are visible on short stalks at the front margin. The background is a blurred, warm-toned surface.
